breakfast.name: Sweet Potato and Coconut
instructions: Boil sweet potatoes
Drizzle with coconut cream
breakfast.description: Boiled sweet potato with coconut cream.

breakfast.name: Cassava Chips
instructions: Slice cassava
Fry in coconut oil
Salt and serve

breakfast.name: Cassava Porridge
instructions: Cassava is the main starch crop on the Solomon Islands
Grated and cooked in coconut milk into a porridge
Sweetened with sugar
A filling, tropical breakfast
breakfast.description: Solomon Islands cassava porridge -- grated cassava cooked in coconut milk with sugar. Cassava is the primary starch crop of the islands. Filling, tropical breakfast.

breakfast.name: Taro with Coconut Cream
instructions: Taro is the ancestral crop of the Pacific -- older than cassava
Boiled until soft and creamy
Served with fresh coconut cream poured over
Simple and deeply traditional
The coconut cream is extracted from freshly grated coconut flesh
breakfast.description: Solomon Islands traditional taro with coconut cream -- taro boiled until soft, served with freshly squeezed coconut cream. Taro is the ancestral Pacific crop. Simple and deeply traditional.

lunch.name: Poi (Taro Pudding)
instructions: Grate taro
Mix with coconut cream
Wrap in banana leaves
Steam 1 hour

lunch.name: Fish in Coconut Milk
instructions: Simmer coconut milk with onion
Add fish, cook 15 min
Squeeze lime

lunch.name: Poi (Fermented Taro)
ingredients: Cooked taro (mashed and fermented overnight to several days)
instructions: Poi is the Polynesian fermented taro paste -- also eaten in Melanesia
Cooked taro is mashed and allowed to ferment
Fresh poi: slightly sweet, pasty
Fermented poi (2+ days): slightly sour, more complex
The consistency: from paste to thin (one-finger, two-finger poi -- by thickness)
Eaten alongside fish or protein
lunch.description: Solomon Islands fermented taro paste -- cooked taro mashed and allowed to ferment, fresh (slightly sweet, thick) or aged (slightly sour, more complex). Eaten alongside fish or protein. The consistency describes it: thick poi needs two fingers; thin poi, one.

lunch.name: Grilled Fish Wrapped in Banana Leaf
instructions: Reef fish cooked in banana leaf packets is the traditional Melanesian cooking method
The fish is marinated with coconut cream and aromatics
Wrapped tightly in banana leaves
Cooked over coals or in the umu (earth oven)
The banana leaf steams the fish in its own juices
lunch.description: Solomon Islands banana leaf-steamed fish -- fresh reef fish marinated with coconut cream, lemon grass, and chilli, wrapped in banana leaves and cooked over coals or in the umu earth oven. The banana leaf creates a steam pouch; the fish cooks in its own juices.

lunch.name: Kokoda (Raw Fish Salad)
ingredients: Fresh white fish (very fresh -- snapper, mahi-mahi)
instructions: Kokoda is the Melanesian raw fish dish -- similar to Samoan oka or ceviche
Fresh fish cut into pieces, marinated in lime juice
The acid cooks the fish
Coconut cream added after -- the richness
Vegetables added and the dish is served cold
lunch.description: Solomon Islands Melanesian raw fish -- fresh fish acid-cooked in lime juice, enriched with coconut cream, tossed with onion, tomato, chilli, and cucumber. Similar to Samoan oka and Fijian kokoda. The coconut cream distinguishes Pacific raw fish from Latin American ceviche.

dinner.name: Motu (Earth Oven)
instructions: Heat stones
Wrap food in banana leaves
Layer over stones
Cover with earth, cook 3 hours

dinner.name: Grilled Fish
instructions: Score, season, grill over coals

dinner.name: Lap Lap (Ground Root Vegetable Pudding)
ingredients: Taro, cassava, or sweet potato (grated raw)
Pork, chicken, or fish (for the filling inside)
instructions: Lap lap is the Solomon Islands national dish
Grated raw taro or cassava mixed with coconut cream
The mixture is spread on banana leaves
Meat or fish is placed in the center
Wrapped tightly and cooked in the umu (earth oven)
A dense, filling dish that takes hours
The umu is dug in the ground, stones heated, then food wrapped in leaves placed inside
dinner.description: Solomon Islands national dish -- grated taro or cassava mixed with coconut cream, wrapped around meat or fish in banana leaves, and slow-cooked in the umu (earth oven: a pit with heated stones). Dense and filling. The umu is used for all major communal cooking.

dinner.name: Coconut Crab
ingredients: Coconut crab (Birgus latro -- the world largest land invertebrate)
instructions: The coconut crab is the world largest land-living arthropod
Found on Pacific islands: it lives on land, climbs coconut trees, eats coconuts
Its claws can crack open a coconut
The meat is rich, sweet, and flavored by its coconut diet
Braised in coconut milk: the coconut-on-coconut combination
dinner.description: Solomon Islands coconut crab -- Birgus latro, the world largest land invertebrate, which lives on land and climbs coconut trees to eat coconuts. The meat is rich, sweet, and coconut-flavored. Braised in coconut milk. Increasingly rare due to overharvesting.

dinner.name: Sweet Potato and Greens
ingredients: Sweet potato (local -- purple or orange varieties)
Tropical greens (sweet potato leaves, spinach, or taro leaves)
instructions: Sweet potato greens are nutritious and commonly eaten in the Pacific
The leaves of the sweet potato plant are cooked alongside the root
Combined with coconut cream
A simple, complete vegetarian meal
dinner.description: Solomon Islands sweet potato with its own leaves -- sweet potato rooted and leafy greens cooked together with coconut cream. Using the whole plant. A simple, complete, vegetarian Pacific meal.

snacks.name: Baked Breadfruit
instructions: Roast over coals 45 min
Peel and serve

snacks.name: Betel Nut (Buai)
instructions: Betel nut chewing is the most widespread social habit in the Solomon Islands and Papua New Guinea
Areca nut: the seed of the areca palm (not the betel plant)
Chewed with betel leaf and lime powder -- the chemical reaction produces the red color and stimulant effect
The lime powder (from crushed coral or shells): activates the arecoline alkaloid
The red saliva: the visible sign of betel nut chewing
A social ritual: buai is offered to guests, shared in villages
Note: betel nut is classified as a Group 1 carcinogen by WHO
snacks.description: Solomon Islands betel nut ritual -- areca nut (buai) chewed with betel leaf and coral lime powder. The chemical reaction produces red saliva and mild stimulant effects. The most widespread social ritual in Melanesia. Offered to guests and shared in villages. Note: classified by WHO as Group 1 carcinogen.

snacks.name: Fresh Papaya
instructions: Papaya grows throughout the Solomon Islands
Eaten fresh with a squeeze of lime
The lime and salt combination: Asian-Pacific style of eating papaya
snacks.description: Solomon Islands fresh papaya -- ripe papaya with lime juice and optional salt or chilli. Papaya grows throughout the islands. Lime and salt with fresh papaya is the Pacific way.

snacks.name: Roasted Breadfruit
instructions: Breadfruit roasted in fire coals
The exterior chars while the interior steams
Eaten as a starchy snack or starch alongside a meal
snacks.description: Solomon Islands roasted breadfruit -- whole breadfruit placed in fire coals until the exterior chars and the interior steams creamy. Eaten as starch or snack, optionally with coconut cream.

desserts.name: Banana in Coconut Cream
instructions: Warm bananas in sweetened coconut cream

desserts.name: Coconut Jam
instructions: Coconut jam (kaya in Southeast Asia) is made from coconut and sugar
Cooked until thick and spreadable
Pandan leaf gives aromatic green flavor
Spread on bread or eaten by spoon
desserts.description: Solomon Islands coconut jam -- fresh grated coconut cooked with sugar and pandan leaf into a thick, aromatic, spreadable jam. Spread on bread or eaten directly.

desserts.name: Banana Baked in Coconut Milk
instructions: Baked banana in coconut milk is a simple Pacific dessert
Bananas baked in sweetened coconut milk
The banana softens further and the coconut milk caramelizes slightly
desserts.description: Solomon Islands baked banana -- ripe bananas baked in sweetened coconut milk with cinnamon until the banana softens and the coconut milk caramelizes slightly. Simple and tropical.

drinks.name: Coconut Water
instructions: Crack open, drink fresh

drinks.name: Betel Nut Spit
instructions: Chew betel nut with lime — not a drink per se but the Islands' stimulant

drinks.name: Fresh Sugarcane Juice
instructions: Sugarcane is grown throughout the Solomon Islands
Pressed through a mill to extract the juice
Fresh, sweet, and fibrous
A splash of lime juice brightens it
drinks.description: Solomon Islands fresh sugarcane juice -- sugarcane pressed through a mill for sweet, fibrous juice, brightened with lime. Sugarcane grows throughout the islands.
